segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so quick check on Benton Parts. They want the proposal today for 74 seats, annual, go-live February 12, and procurement asked for net 45 instead of net 30.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Is that the same package we talked through, support plus the reporting add-on?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, $48,600 for the year before tax. The annoying part is getting the actual proposal out. I had to update the account in the CRM, then put the same 74 seats and start date into the pricing sheet, then retype the discount and billing terms in the quote tool, then copy it again into the approval form for deal desk, and then the billing tool wants the legal name, address, PO contact, all of it again. It’s the same customer info at every stop, and if one field is off, it kicks back. I started it yesterday at 3:00, got one approval this morning, and I’m still waiting because the contract workspace doesn’t pull any of that over either.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Ugh. For the discount, what did you put in front of deal desk?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Twelve percent. List was $55,200. I noted they’re replacing two smaller tools and they’ll add the warehouse team in Q3 if rollout goes clean.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: That should be fine. Did legal already approve the net 45, or is that still pending?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Still pending. I flagged it as customer paper only for the PO terms, not their full services agreement. Their buyer, Melissa, said they can sign our order form if finance sees the invoice language today.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay, send me the draft before it goes out. I’ll sanity-check the seat count and the February 12 service date.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. If deal desk clears by 2:00, I’ll send it to Melissa and copy their ops lead. Otherwise I’ll give her a heads-up that it’s coming first thing tomorrow.
